content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"no","applies_why":"The judge text does not count a cited verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it says [CR2] G answers the rows and leaves the sign's sense open.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"'counts as an unanswered witness': whether the rule reaches a judge's statement that a round answers rows and leaves the link underdetermined, or only reaches counting a cited verse toward a broken link as unanswered.","why":"Because the judge text treats the rows as answered and leaves the link underdetermined, it does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link."}
